note: Bodies the Solar System mode is known to work on (detected in a single SPHEREx pass, with a background control: S/N >= 5 in at least two detector bands, or >= 50 when saturation leaves one). 'passes' lists the passes measured and their best per-band S/N. Written with Claude Code.

bodies.name: Haumea
bodies.blurb: An egg-shaped dwarf planet beyond Neptune that spins once every four hours, coated in bright crystalline water ice.
bodies.composition: crystalline water ice with deep 1.5 and 2.0 um bands; band depths 0.36 +- 0.05 at 1.50 um and 0.55 +- 0.05 at 2.00 um against the local continuum (Dumas et al. 2011, arXiv:1101.2102); a 1:1 crystalline/amorphous water-ice mixture (Pinilla-Alonso et al. 2009, arXiv:0803.1080)
bodies.composition_ref: Dumas et al. 2011, A&A, arXiv:1101.2102; Pinilla-Alonso et al. 2009, A&A 496, 547, arXiv:0803.1080; Gourgeot et al. 2016, A&A, arXiv:1605.04145

bodies.name: Makemake
bodies.blurb: One of the brightest worlds in the Kuiper Belt, a dwarf planet covered in methane ice.
bodies.composition: methane ice dominates, with strong CH4 bands through the near-infrared (Grundy et al. 2024, JWST NIRSpec, arXiv:2309.05085)

bodies.name: Eris
bodies.blurb: The most massive known dwarf planet, now almost 100 times farther from the Sun than Earth, with a methane-ice surface.
bodies.composition: methane ice dominates, with N2 ice indicated near 4.2 um (Grundy et al. 2024, JWST NIRSpec, arXiv:2309.05085)

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.blurb: Pluto and its large moon Charon, unresolved by SPHEREx and measured as one source.
